questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study in Europe for financial reasons (Erasmus+). It was also crucial for me that i could take some of my mandatory elective courses at my host university because my bachelor is quite limited in terms of number of elective courses. Lastly, i have always loved Spain and the culture, so i wanted to live there and learn more.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, it was a great experience, but i found i hard to meet new people.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: We received a lot of mails from our host university with the necessary information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They have a Buddy program, but i did not receive one by mistake. Luckily, i went there with a friend so we just used his buddy if needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not hard, but not easy either. there is a lot of scam in Spain, which makes it hard.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Educate yourself on the area - we ended up staying in one of the sketchier areas.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Housing can be found in facebook group (i found my apartment there) and on idealista, but be aware of agency fees on idealista as they are a lot

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: we had a lot of trouble with our courses in the beginning, and because the faculty was on summer break until 31. August (day before arrival), we could not get any help before arriving. It brought a lot of stress and uncertainty, and then we got there in the first week of september, we were told to wait patiently as they were sorting out the waiting lists. This took them a couple of weeks, so we missed the first 2-3 weeks of 3 courses out of 5.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Courses at my host institution are assigned on a first-come, first-served basis. We were registrating for courses through our Online Learning Agreement which requires a preapproval of courses from sending institution. I did my preapproval as fast as i possibly could, but because the process of approving took so long, i still ended up on a waitlist on a course that was necessary for me to have.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: not much, i was told to wait and that they could not guarantee me a spot (it took 2-3 weeks)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up being successful in the end

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Only very few does not get their waitlists resolved, so be patient even though it is stressful

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was great

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level a lot easier than my own university

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They have continuous evaluation at my host university, and UCPH have 100% final exams. I chose to waive the continuous evaluation in two courses, because this is the form i am familiar with.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Macroeconomics (Economics Degree), International Economics, Regional Economics, Economic History of Contemporary Spain, and Institutions and Economic Regulation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: i would recommend taking Macroeconomics as this will count as Macroeconomics III, and International Economics a prioritized elective. I would also recommend Regional Economics, because there is no sit-in exam (its a project).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were non, not even a canteen

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: non, or maybe i just dont know

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: travel to near by cities, hiking, surfing, explore the food culture

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: travel

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I have been to Spain many times before, so it was easy for me

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: learn Spanish, because most cant speak english

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: just the language. They speak basque and Spanish, so english is their 3rd language

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) try find accommodation there you have to live with many (4-5) international students, because this is the easiest way to meet people. 2) be patient with courses, it will be resolved. 3) and travel, the basque country is beautiful and is even more special outside of Bilbao

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: explore new cultures and travel while still taking relevant courses

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and make friends

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
